stem:
The diagram shows point $P$, line $L$, and points $F$ and $Q$ on $L$. Segment $PF$ meets $L$ at right angles. Segment $PQ$ is drawn dashed.

Which claim about the perpendicular projection of $P$ onto $L$ is correct?

options.text: Point $F$ is the perpendicular projection of $P$ onto $L$, and $PF$ is the shortest segment from $P$ to $L$.
Segment $PQ$ is the perpendicular projection of $P$ onto $L$.
Every segment from $P$ to a point on $L$ is a perpendicular projection onto $L$.
Point $F$ is the projection of $P$ onto $L$ only because $F$ is labelled on $L$.

teacher.key_rationale: The perpendicular from $P$ to $L$ meets $L$ at $F$, so $F$ is the foot of the perpendicular projection and $PF$ is shortest. $PQ$ is not perpendicular, not every segment to $L$ is a projection, and the label alone does not define the projection.
teacher.figure_note: Line L with foot F of the perpendicular from P; dashed PQ to another point on L.
